q: An ISR produces into a full queue. Which line is correct inside the ISR?
options: `k_msgq_put(&q, &s, K_FOREVER);`: wait until the thread makes room
`k_msgq_put(&q, &s, K_MSEC(1));`: a short wait is fine
explain: An ISR can never wait, so any timeout other than `K_NO_WAIT` is a bug (the simulator stops you, and real Zephyr asserts or misbehaves). With `K_NO_WAIT` a full queue returns `-ENOMSG` at once, and you apply your drop policy and **count it**. The queue is already safe to use from an ISR without a lock, and mutexes can't be used in ISRs anyway.

q: A balance-control loop consumes gyro samples from an 8-slot queue. The consumer is sometimes stalled for 30 ms. Which full-queue policy fits, and why?
options: Drop-newest: it keeps the history in order
Drop-oldest: after a stall the controller should see the freshest data, not 30 ms-old readings
Block the ISR until there's room
Make the queue 1 deep so it never overflows
explain: For control, the value of a sample decays fast. Drop-oldest (`get` the oldest, then `put` the new one) means the queue always holds the **newest** 8 samples, so the controller resumes on fresh data. Drop-newest is right for logs and protocols, where order and history matter more. Blocking is impossible in an ISR. A queue that's 1 deep still overflows; it just loses more.

q: 1 kHz samples, a queue of depth 8 with drop-oldest, and a consumer stalled for exactly 20 ms with an empty queue at the start. How many samples get dropped during the stall? (Assume exactly 20 arrive.)
explain: 20 arrive and only 8 fit, so 20 − 8 = **12** are dropped: the 12 oldest. The 8 newest survive, and when the consumer wakes, the oldest sample it sees is about 8 ms old. Drop-newest would drop the same *number*, but keep the 8 *oldest*, which are up to 20 ms stale. Same count, very different usefulness.

options: Messages are copied into the queue's own static buffer, so the producer can reuse its struct right away
`k_msgq_get(..., K_NO_WAIT)` on an empty queue returns -ENOMSG
Each queue can carry messages of different sizes
If a thread is already waiting in `k_msgq_get`, a put can hand the message directly to that thread
explain: Message size is fixed per queue (`K_MSGQ_DEFINE(name, msg_size, max_msgs, align)`). For variable-length data, use `k_fifo`/`k_pipe` or a buffer pool. Messages are copied in and out of static storage, `-ENOMSG` signals full or empty with `K_NO_WAIT`, and a waiting receiver can get the message copied straight into its buffer, which is why a preempted consumer can end up holding one stale sample.
